key_insight: FEVessel adapts a label-free pretrained finite element framework to 3D pressure vessels, enabling mesh-independent elasticity prediction and solver warm-starting without FEM-generated labels.
engineering_relevance: It can cut simulation cost and avoid mesh-repair bottlenecks for industrial pressure-vessel analysis across varying materials, geometries, loads, and poor-quality meshes.
method: Encode each vessel as a point cloud with coordinate, material, and load channels.
Pretrain a Transolver on total potential energy instead of supervised FEM labels.
Use the prediction to warm-start algebraic multigrid iterative solves.
evidence_signal: The model reports 1.35% relative displacement error, 2.07% strain error, and a 9.2× wall-clock speedup with AMG iterations reduced from 195 to 18 at 10^-3 tolerance.
watch_item: Results are promising but still depend on careful solver integration and point-cloud representation choices, especially when transferring across mesh densities or highly degenerate elements.
paper_title: FEVessel: Mesh-Independent Analysis of 3D Pressure Vessels with the Label-Free Pretrained Finite Element Method
